finding: Round 6 replaced TEST-14's lying doc with an equally false one. The new text claims 'read_prompt_file exercises whichever is live (on Linux, openat2), and open_confined_fallback is then driven DIRECTLY - so removing either anchor guard turns this red on Linux', and FIX_ROUND-6.md records 'TEST-14 now drives open_confined_fallback DIRECTLY, plus a control that an ordinary root still reads through it'. EVIDENCE: `grep -n open_confined_fallback validate.rs` returns 1334, 1345, 1352 (the impl and its callers) and 2404 - which IS the doc comment itself. The test body (lines 2407-2434) calls only read_prompt_file, twice; there is no direct fallback call and no such control. MUTATION PROOF (tree restored after): (a) neutering the FALLBACK anchor guard - `std::fs::symlink_metadata(root)` -> `std::fs::metadata(root)` in open_confined_fallback, which makes a symlinked root pass is_dir() - leaves `cargo test --lib -p ziee -- workflow::validate` at 43 passed; 0 failed, with read_prompt_file_refuses_a_bundle_root_that_became_a_symlink explicitly listed as ok; (b) neutering the LINUX anchor guard (dropping libc::O_NOFOLLOW from the custom_flags at validate.rs:1279) turns the SAME test RED (42 passed; 1 failed, panic at validate.rs:2426). So exactly one of the two guards is falsified, the fallback's is not, and the round that was convened specifically to stop this comment from lying re-asserted the lie and recorded TEST-14 as PASS in TEST_RESULTS.md:34.

The behavioural narrowing was applied to the resolver but NOT to the live model-facing contract. `dir_prop` still reads 'The workspace subdir (relative to /home/sandboxuser) holding workflow.yaml + any scripts/ you wrote with the code_sandbox tools.' and RUN_FROM_WORKSPACE's description still says 'Write workflow.yaml (+ scripts/) into /home/sandboxuser/<dir>/ first' - no `pattern`, no maxLength, no prose stating that <dir> must now be exactly one path component. 'relative to /home/sandboxuser' plainly reads as 'a relative path', which is what the code now refuses. The three schemas (run/validate/save) all reuse this same unchanged dir_prop (tools.rs:252/267/278), and parse_workspace_args (tools.rs:513-524) validates only non-emptiness, so the constraint exists nowhere the model can see before calling. Self-correction IS possible (see the rejected row on error text), but the schema advertising something the code rejects is the definition of a contract break.

`normals != 1` also rejects `dir = "."` / `"./"`, a case neither the plan, the comment, FIX_ROUND-6.md, nor the error message accounts for. EVIDENCE: compiled a standalone probe over `Path::components()` (/data/pbya/ziee/tmp/audit-r7b/comp.rs): '.' and './' yield normals=0, so they hit the new guard; before this commit they were accepted (the loop tolerated Component::CurDir and there was no count) and resolved to the conversation workspace root itself. That root is `runner::workflow_workspace_root().join(conv)` = code_sandbox's `state.workspace_root/<conv>` (runner.rs:1782-1791 vs code_sandbox/handlers.rs:1130) - i.e. exactly `/home/sandboxuser`, the sandbox's HOME and default cwd, where `write_file` writes by default (code_sandbox/handlers.rs:1300). So the most frictionless authoring flow (write_file('workflow.yaml'), then run_from_workspace with dir='.') silently regressed. Worse, the security rationale does not apply to it: with dir='.' the anchor's final component is the conversation UUID directory, which is the bind MOUNT POINT and cannot be renamed from inside the sandbox - '.' is strictly safer than the single-component case the rule permits. And the emitted message, "'dir' must name a single directory directly inside the conversation workspace, not a nested path", misdiagnoses a zero-component input as a nested one.

The round-6 commit adds a workspace.rs entry with 7 angles (security, correctness, concurrency, tests-quality, maintainability, design-conformance, wired-and-behaving). EVIDENCE: `git diff origin/feat/agent-core..a67317c2a --stat -- workflow/workspace.rs` is EMPTY - the file was untouched by the branch until the round-6 fix created it - and no ledger row in any round has file == 'src-app/server/src/modules/workflow/workspace.rs' (the sole grep hit, in ledger-round3-a.jsonl, is a row whose `file` is validate.rs and which merely cites workspace.rs as prior art). 'wired-and-behaving' and 'design-conformance' appear in no round-5/6 ledger at all. The same applies to the tools.rs hunk at 687-689 (the validate_collecting_async swap), which is inherited coverage from the pre-fix tools.rs entry even though the hunk was authored in response to round 6's finding. Net: 6 workspace.rs rows and 1 tools.rs row in AUDIT_COVERAGE.tsv satisfy lifecycle-check's >=3-distinct-angles gate on attributions that could not have occurred.

The evidence that answers the ITEM-18 backward-compatibility CONCERN is a green count that cannot distinguish 'ran' from 'returned at line 1'. TEST_RESULTS.md:44-49 claims '46 passed; 0 failed - including t4_run_from_workspace_drives_real_llm_step, t4_llm_agentically_runs_and_saves_workflow and t4_workspace_verbs_honor_approval_mode, i.e. the real-LLM workspace verbs whose `dir` argument the restriction narrows', and PLAN_AUDIT.md:146-150 leans on exactly that number ('the concern is answered by measurement'). EVIDENCE: all three tests open with `if std::env::var("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY").is_err() { return; }` (workspace_test.rs:841, 900, 1031) and count as passed when they self-skip; this worktree contains NO src-app/server/tests/.env.test (the file the project's own run recipe sources), so the documented default state of the tree is key-absent. Neither artifact records whether the key was exported, which is the one fact that makes the number mean anything.

Persisted pre-change state is not considered anywhere in the branch. run_from_workspace stamps the authored `dir` into the tool result as `structuredContent.workspace_dir` (tools.rs:640-648); that block is persisted in chat history, and WorkflowWorkspaceRunCard reads it back (`sc?.workspace_dir`) to drive 'Save to my workflows' (POST /api/workflows/workspace-save) and 'Download .tar.gz' (GET /api/workflows/workspace-export). Both endpoints re-resolve the same string through resolve_conversation_workspace_dir (handlers/dev.rs:1579 and 1624). A run authored before this commit with a nested dir therefore leaves a permanently-rendered pair of buttons that now fail with 400 WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_BAD_DIR, surfaced to the user as 'Save failed: ...' / 'Download failed (400)'. Same for the model re-invoking run_from_workspace on a dir it used earlier in the conversation. There is no back-compat allowance, no migration, and PLAN_AUDIT.md's dismissal ('no fixture or caller in the tree uses a nested dir') reasons only about in-tree call sites, not about strings already stored in users' message rows.

The function's own public doc comment is now incomplete for the rule that most surprises a caller. Lines 44-48 still say only 'Rejects absolute paths, `..`, and (via canonicalize) symlink escapes.' The single-component requirement - the change's entire point, and the one rejection an existing caller will hit - is documented only in an inline comment in the middle of the body (73-82) and in the error string. FIX_ROUND-6.md claims 'The function doc no longer claims more than the guard delivers'; that statement is true of open_confined's inline comment in validate.rs, not of this function's doc, which is the one a caller reads via rustdoc/hover.

The two tests that exercise the new rule are the only ones in the module that write into a REAL, shared, process-global directory instead of a tempdir. Both build `runner::workflow_workspace_root().join(conv)` and `fs::create_dir_all(..).unwrap()`; with no code_sandbox state configured in a lib-test process that root is `std::env::temp_dir().join("ziee-workflows")` (runner.rs:1789) - confirmed by the mutation run's panic text `/tmp/ziee-workflows/<uuid>/proj/flow`. On this host that directory currently holds 3096 entries (mode 0755, single owner), so (a) cleanup is best-effort and is SKIPPED entirely on the failing path, since `let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&base)` sits after the `.unwrap()`/`.unwrap_err()` that panics, and (b) on a shared or multi-user box a foreign-owned /tmp/ziee-workflows turns `create_dir_all(...).unwrap()` into an environmental panic that reads as a code failure. Every other filesystem test in this branch (validate.rs's TEST-3/12/13/14) uses `tempdir()`.

No integration-tier assertion of the narrowing, so the thing the model actually receives is unpinned. t2_run_from_workspace_rejects_traversal already iterates a bad-dir list ['../../etc', '/etc', 'a/../../b'] and asserts structuredContent.code == WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_BAD_DIR at the MCP surface; adding 'proj/flow' there was a one-token change and was not made. As a result nothing asserts that the new rejection reaches the model as an isError tool result (rather than a JSON-RPC error), nor that its code/message are the self-correctable ones - the only coverage is the unit test on the resolver.
